title: Other single cases
question: He speaks, media or fans, and other one-off splits.

subgroups.name: he_speaks: what counts as his words
subgroups.note: Both tune side. #491 is made of long direct quotes; one reader's no has no reading behind it in the notes and looks like a slip. #823 is the real case: his Instagram post is paraphrased, and the only quote of his is two words recalled from after his previous win.

subgroups.name: source: his words are off the page, or a fan line inside a journalist's piece
subgroups.note: Two different source problems. #740 (test) is a video page: the caption says he talks with UFC.com after his win, but none of his words are saved; the readers went three ways. #823 (tune) carries the same doubt in its notes (the result came from his post, so 'himself' was called arguable) and is the tune-side witness. #654 (check): the only thing about him is a readers' poll figure inside a staff-picks page.

subgroups.name: fact: a statement announced without its content
subgroups.note: Tune side. A one-line stub: he addressed his loss in a letter to his son. Nothing of the letter is given. Readers split no_fact / personal_life, and firmness none / official_or_done with it. This is backlog rule 1 (parked by Anton on #856) in a second article.

readings: he_speaks: yes whenever a direct quote of his stands in the saved text, however short and whenever he said it; a post or interview only mentioned or paraphrased is no.
he_speaks: yes only for words he said for this story; a two-word fragment recalled from an earlier occasion, or a paraphrased post, is no.

source: who the saved text shows speaking or acting; a video or post the text only names as where the news came from does not make him the source, so a bare result is no_one; and a fan poll quoted by a journalist is fans, because the question asks who spoke, not who published.

source: the page's nature decides; a page of his interview is himself even with no words saved (or promotion, because UFC.com states the result), and a staff-picks page is media even when the only line about him is the readers' vote.
fact: an article that says he made a statement but gives none of it carries no fact (no_fact, firmness none); a letter is a place where things are said, and nothing said is saved.
fact: writing a letter to his son about his loss is itself a life event, so personal_life, and it happened, so official_or_done.
signals: Quotation marks or guillemets around words attributed to him (“...”, «...»): his words are on the page.
A speech verb with his name and no quote after it ('talks with UFC.com', 'reported this on Instagram', 'addressed his loss in a letter'): his words are off the page.
A recall marker before the quote ('Нагадаємо' / 'recall', 'then', 'after his previous win'): the quote is from an earlier occasion, not this story.
Video-player furniture ('This video is not available', 'Up next', 'Continue watching') making up most of the text: the page's content is a video the text does not hold.
Scores and a verdict with no speaker ('30-27, 30-27, 29-28', 'unanimous decision'): the text carries an event, source no_one.
A line labelled as readers or fans ('Readers 148-65: ... Donchenko (71%)') next to a line about the outlet's own staff ('our 11 editors'): who made the pick is written down.
The statement is named but not summarised ('addressed his loss ... in a letter') and no sentence says what it said: there is no content to classify.
Comment-policy or subscription boilerplate making up most of the saved text: a stub, whatever it is labelled.

rules.name: any-quote-counts
rules.subgroup: he_speaks: what counts as his words
rules.text: he_speaks is yes when a direct quote of his stands in the saved text, however short and whenever he said it. A post, letter, interview or video that the text only mentions or paraphrases, with none of his words, is no.

examples.why: Long direct quotes on his camp, his French and Soriano: yes under any reading; the one no has no reading behind it.
His post is paraphrased, but two of his words stand in guillemets («хороші друзі»), recalled from after his last win: yes by the letter of the question.

rules.name: words-on-the-page
rules.subgroup: source: his words are off the page, or a fan line inside a journalist's piece
rules.text: Source is who the saved text shows speaking or acting. A post, interview or video that the text only names as where the news came from, or as the page's content, without giving his words, does not make him the source: answer for what the text carries (a bare result is no_one, act reports_an_event). Where his speaking is itself the news (he addressed his loss in a letter), he is the source even without a quote.

examples.why: The text carries the result with scores; his Instagram post is only where the outlet got it, and his callout is a wish: no_one, as the readers agreed.
The contrast: the whole news is that he spoke (a letter about his loss), so himself even though none of the letter is saved.

rules.name: who-spoke-not-who-published
rules.subgroup: source: his words are off the page, or a fan line inside a journalist's piece
rules.text: Source is who made the words or the pick, not who published them. A fan poll, reader vote or fan post quoted inside a journalist's piece is fans; the journalist's own pick, analysis or report is media. When the saved text holds only the fan figure about him, source is fans and act predicts_his_fight.

examples.why: The only line about him is 'Readers 148-65: ... Donchenko (71%)'; the staff's own picks are cut off after 'Here are the results:'.

rules.name: no-content-no-fact
rules.subgroup: fact: a statement announced without its content
rules.text: When the article says he made a statement, post or letter but gives none of what it said, fact is no_fact and firmness none: a statement is a place where things are said, and nothing said is saved. The yes/no news questions are no.

examples.why: One deck line, 'addressed his loss ... in a letter penned to his son', then comment-policy boilerplate; what the letter said is not on the page.

why: All four write down the readers' majorities, so they cost no relabels; what they buy is a line the next reader can apply without judgement. The cost of any-quote-counts is that two recalled words make a yes, so he_speaks says nothing about whether he is the source (#823 is yes with source no_one); the stricter 'fresh words only' reading would flip #823 to no and would need a recall marker in the text each time. words-on-the-page settles a video page as no_one, which drops the only signal the page has (that it is his interview); the backlog's rule 4 flag for unsaved content still applies to such pages. no-content-no-fact is backlog rule 1, which Anton parked on #856; adopting it here un-parks it, and it leaves #647 with source himself and he_speaks no, the pair the classifier's rule 2 would break on.

per_article.491: Direct quotes throughout, so he_speaks yes; nothing else was disputed.
per_article.823: Two quoted words of his stand in the text, so he_speaks yes; the result with scores is the news and his post is only the channel, so source no_one, act reports_an_event.
per_article.654: Only the readers' poll figure is about him, so source fans; the staff picks are not in the saved text.
per_article.740: The caption names his interview but holds none of his words, so he_speaks no and the text carries only the result: source no_one, act reports_an_event; UFC.com stating its own result is still an event, not a promotion statement (unsure: a case for promotion exists).
per_article.647: He is named as having spoken, so source himself and act speaks_of_himself, but none of the letter is saved: he_speaks no, fact no_fact, firmness none.

unsure: #740: source no_one over promotion. UFC.com is both the outlet and the promotion; the guide's 'official records' could cover a UFC.com result caption. Treated the same as #823 (an outlet relaying a result) for consistency.
#491's lone no on he_speaks: no reader note supports it, so it is read as a slip rather than a boundary.
The he_speaks recommendation follows the guide's literal wording; the stricter reading may serve the product better if he_speaks is meant to flag articles where he says something new.
